SMTO-HTTP-0046 — The service uses a sign-in type SMTO doesn't support

GUID: 6dde6db3-5464-485d-a3c0-e35ec163902f
Slug: http-feature-unsupported
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service's sign-in gave SMTO a special kind of access pass that it can't use. SMTO only supports the common Bearer type.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the service's owner, or check its documentation, whether this account or app can be given standard Bearer tokens. SMTO can only use Bearer access passes, and many services can issue them on request.
  2. If the service offers another sign-in option, such as an API key, change Authentication on the HTTP connection in Parameter Store to that option and fill it in. A different supported sign-in type avoids the unsupported access pass.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. When it shows Authenticated, run the task again. This confirms the new sign-in works before the task uses it.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; this service may need a different tool. Don't treat the unusable sign-in as successful.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OAuth token response declared token_type DPoP or MAC; native HTTP supports Bearer tokens only.

What this means

  • OAuth token_type is DPoP or MAC, while the current provider supports Bearer tokens only. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth token_type is DPoP or MAC, while the current provider supports Bearer tokens only.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the provider's documented token type; installing unrelated packages does not add this unimplemented protocol.

How to fix it

  • Configure the OAuth client or authorization server to issue Bearer tokens, or switch the profile to another supported auth type (API key, basic or session login). DPoP- or MAC-bound tokens require a tool that implements those protocols.
  • Use a documented Bearer-compatible flow or an implementation that supports the required token protocol.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported Bearer flow is deliberately configured, or a tool implementing the required protocol is used.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
